items.name: Congruent Supplements Theorem
items.text: angles supplementary to the same (or congruent) angles are congruent.

items.name: Congruent Complements Theorem
items.text: angles complementary to the same (or congruent) angles are congruent.

items.name: Triangle Angle Sum Theorem
items.text: interior angles of a triangle add to 180°.

items.name: Exterior Angle Theorem
items.text: an exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.

items.name: Isosceles Triangle Theorem
items.text: if two sides are congruent, the angles opposite them are congruent (and the converse is true).

sections.title: Parallel lines cut by a transversal
rows: Linear pair (next to each other on one line)
sections.note: Note: The converses also hold: if any of these relationships is true, the lines are parallel.

sections.title: Solving for x with parallel lines
steps: Name the angle pair (corresponding, alternate interior, and so on).
Congruent pair: set the expressions equal. Supplementary pair: set their sum = 180.
Solve for x, then plug x back in to find the angle measure if asked.

examples.title: Congruent example
examples.text: Corresponding angles are (2x + 41)° and 51°. So 2x + 41 = 51, 2x = 10, x = 5.

examples.title: Supplementary example
examples.text: Same-side interior angles are (3x + 10)° and (5x + 10)°. So 3x + 10 + 5x + 10 = 180, 8x = 160, x = 20 (angles are 70° and 110°).

sections.tip: Quick check: both angles look acute (or both obtuse)? They're congruent, so set them equal. One acute and one obtuse? They're supplementary, so add to 180.

sections.title: Triangle congruence shortcuts

sections.tip: Memory trick: the letter order matters. In SAS the A is in the middle, so the angle must sit between the two sides. Never rely on SSA or AAA.

blocks.title: CPCTC
blocks.text: Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles are Congruent. Use it after you prove the triangles congruent, to conclude that a specific side or angle matches.

blocks.title: Where to find the pieces
items: Vertical angles at an X: Vertical Angles Theorem.
Midpoint or bisector: gives congruent segments or angles.
Parallel lines: alternate interior angles are congruent.
Perpendicular lines: right angles, and all right angles are congruent.

proofs.title: SAS with a midpoint
proofs.given: M is the midpoint of AD and of BC (segments cross at M).
rows: 1) M is the midpoint of AD and BC

proofs.title: ASA with an angle bisector + CPCTC

sections.title: Proof-writing checklist
items: Mark the diagram with everything from the Given (tick marks, arcs, right-angle boxes).
Look for free pieces: shared sides, vertical angles, parallel-line angles.
Pick the shortcut that matches what you have (SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, HL).
Name the triangles in matching vertex order (△ABC ≅ △DEF means A↔D, B↔E, C↔F).
Every statement needs a reason: Given, definition, postulate, or theorem.
Need a side or angle after congruence? Finish with CPCTC.
